default.message: Use the `read` tool instead of cat/head/tail. It provides better context and handles binary files.
Use the `grep` tool instead of grep/rg. It respects .gitignore and provides structured output.
Use the `glob` tool instead of find/fd. It respects .gitignore and is faster for glob patterns.
Use the `edit` tool instead of sed -i. It provides diff preview and fuzzy matching.
Use the `edit` tool instead of perl -i. It provides diff preview and fuzzy matching.
Use the `edit` tool instead of awk -i inplace. It provides diff preview and fuzzy matching.

Use the `write` tool instead of echo/cat redirection. It handles encoding and provides confirmation. `write` replaces the whole file; to append to an existing file, use `edit` to insert after its last line.
Use `bash` with `name` instead of nohup or background shell syntax so the service stays observable and managed.
Use `bash` with `name` for services, watchers, and debuggers; inspect with `read proc://<name>`.
Use `bash` with `name` for watch mode so its output, input, and lifecycle stay managed.

Switch the task tool to its batch shape: one call carries { context, tasks[] } — one subagent per item, with an optional per-item agent (defaulting to the session spawn-policy agent), per-item isolation, and a required shared context prepended to every assignment. With async.enabled=true, each spawn runs as an independent background agent with the normal idle/parked lifecycle; otherwise the call blocks for merged results. Disable to restore the flat single-spawn schema.

Spawns take ordered `steps` instead of one `task`: the subagent gets the first step, then each next one once it finishes the previous; past 4 steps, earlier messages carry two or more. The last step's result is the task's result.

Expose outputSchema/schemaMode on the task tool and honor agent output schemas; a subagent with a schema returns its result through the yield tool, validated against it. Off: task subagents ignore schemas, except agents whose definition sets structured: true. A subagent without a schema has no yield tool and returns its final message. Eval agent()/workpool spawns always honor schemas.

Start each batch subagent as soon as its tasks[] item finishes streaming instead of waiting for the whole task call. Launched agents are aborted if the finished call fails validation, is blocked, or its arguments change. Requires auto-allowed task approval and no extension tool lifecycle handlers.
Expose the optional effort parameter on task spawns, allowing callers to override each subagent's thinking level

Whether a subagent call may pick its model with one exact provider/model-id[@upstream][:level] selector. An @upstream pin is part of the model identity and is supported only by aggregators. Only models the configuration already routes to are accepted. Project settings can turn it off but not on, and never approve a model.

Exact selectors: `provider/model-id`, including `@upstream` only for a pinned OpenRouter/Vercel route (e.g. `openrouter/x@y`). When set, a per-call model must also be listed here. Empty: every model the configuration grants. A project list can only narrow this one.
Maximum number of subagents running concurrently

Maximum worker threads for subagents. Up to 8 concurrent subagents run on the main thread; at 9 one worker joins, and one more each time the count doubles (18, 36, 72). Workers stop a minute after no subagent is live in them; 0 keeps every subagent on the main thread
Run LSP formatting and diagnostics on subagent edits. Off by default to keep subagents cheap; the lsp tool stays available to them either way.
Let other omp instances in this folder read agent outputs and send messages that can wake agents
How many levels deep subagents can spawn their own subagents

Hard wall-clock limit per subagent (ms). 0 disables it. Defense-in-depth against provider-side stream hangs that escape the inference-layer watchdog; triggers a normal subagent abort with a 'timed out' reason.

Ask a working subagent, through a cached side request like /btw, to estimate how complete its task is: after 2, 5, 10 and 30 more minutes, then hourly. The estimate shows next to the subagent in wait and task views. Only subagents spawned by the main agent of an interactive session are asked; print, RPC, ACP and SDK runs never probe.
How long an idle subagent stays live in memory before being parked to disk (ms). Parked agents are revived automatically when messaged or resumed. 0 keeps idle agents live until exit.

Soft per-subagent request budget (assistant requests per run). Crossing it injects a wrap-up steering notice (see task.softRequestBudgetNotice); at 1.5x the budget the run is force-stopped and the agent must hand back its partial findings. 0 disables the guard. Bundled scout/sonic agents cap out at a lower built-in budget, so a value below that cap still applies to them. A task.agentSoftRequestBudget entry replaces this budget for the agent it names.
Inject one steering notice when a subagent crosses its soft request budget, asking it to wrap up before the 1.5x forced-yield stop.

Maximum reasoning effort allowed for the task tool's per-spawn effort hint or a per-call model. An explicit `:level` is clamped to the highest supported effort at or below this ceiling, and an omitted `:level` inherits the agent's thinking level capped at this value; cold revival re-applies the cap. Unset, `:inherit` and `:off` keep their existing meaning. A per-call model must support an effort at or below this ceiling; the default preserves the model's full range.

Arm prewalk for the bundled generic `task` subagent: it starts on its resolved model, plans and begins the implementation, then hands off to the 'smol' role at its first edit/write. JSON object mapping model roles, model selectors ("provider/model-id"), or provider wildcards ("provider/*") to ordered fallback selectors, e.g. {"default":["openai/gpt-4o-mini"],"google-antigravity/*":["google/*","google-vertex/*"]}. Model-oriented keys apply whenever that model/provider is active, regardless of role; a "provider/*" entry keeps the failing model's id and swaps the provider. An id-prefixed wildcard ("openrouter/google/*") re-prefixes the failing model's bare id (google-antigravity/gemini-x -> openrouter/google/gemini-x) and, used as a key, matches only that provider's ids under the prefix. A fallback entry may carry an explicit thinking suffix ("provider/model:low", ":high", ":max", ":off"); a bare entry inherits the failing turn's effort, and "provider/*" entries always inherit.
